newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain banks in shape to face Euro challenges - Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Spain banks in shape to face Euro challenges - Rojo.

text.p: Spanish banks are in good shape to face the tougher competition that the launch of the single European currency will bring, Bank of Spain Governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Tuesday.

In an address accompanying the central bank's annual report, Rojo said that by breaking down currency barriers, the euro will do away with many of the reasons behind the segmenting of Europe's banking market, forcing heightened competition in all countries.
"Fortunately, the Spanish banking system faces this situation from a favourable starting point," Rojo said.

Non-performing loans, which rose to worrying levels in the last recession, have improved noticeably since. The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans has now fallen to a level near its historic minimum, Rojo said.
The containment of operating costs, begun in past years, also continued in 1996, he added.

"These favourable tendencies, which intensified in the first quarter of 1997, have allowed financial institutions to maintain profitability levels both in terms of balance sheets as well as shareholders' funds, that compare satisfactorily with the results of other banking systems," Rojo said.

Nonetheless, Spanish banks must use the time remaining until the euro's launch as well as possible, given that its launch means heightened competition amidst lower interest rates than those to which the banks here are accustomed.

"During the first years of monetary union there will probably be specific competition to satisfy financial service demand in euros...Those entities that have made the effort to adapt with alacrity will be in the best shape to satisfy demand for services in euros and raise their market share," he said.
